title: Symmetry and Monotonicity of y = (-x)^(2/3)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Describe the graph of y = (-x)^(2/3), identify any symmetry, and specify the intervals where the function is increasing and where it is decreasing.
finalAnswer: \text{Symmetric about the } y\text{-axis; Decreasing on } (-\infty, 0]; \text{ Increasing on } [0, \infty)

steps.title: Rewrite the Fractional Power and Test Symmetry
steps.explanation: Because cube roots are defined for all real numbers and (-x)^2 = x^2, the function is defined on (-inf, inf) and satisfies f(-x) = f(x). Therefore, it is an even function symmetric about the y-axis.
steps.why: Squaring -x eliminates the negative sign before taking the real cube root.

steps.title: Analyze Monotonicity on [0, inf) and (-inf, 0]
steps.explanation: For x >= 0, x^2 is increasing and the cube root is increasing, so x^(2/3) is increasing on [0, inf). For x <= 0, x^2 is decreasing, so x^(2/3) is decreasing on (-inf, 0].
steps.why: The cube root function u^(1/3) is strictly increasing on R, so it preserves the monotonicity of u = x^2 on each half-line.

steps.title: Summarize Graph Features
steps.mathExpression: \text{Symmetric about } y\text{-axis; Decreasing on } (-\infty, 0]; \text{ Increasing on } [0, \infty)
steps.explanation: The graph forms a symmetric cusp at the origin (0, 0), passing through (-1, 1), (0, 0), and (1, 1), decreasing on (-inf, 0] and increasing on [0, inf).
steps.why: Even symmetry reflects the increasing right branch on [0, inf) into a decreasing left branch on (-inf, 0].
